notes: Shard + incremental index required — they expect continuous ingest from EHR + RIS feeds.
PHI constraint: no egress, all raw PHI must stay inside hospital VPC. Quote from CISO: 'No PHI leaves our networks; full audit trail required.'
Current prototype: embeddings generated with open-encoder, 100 dim vectors; local vector store on k-NN. Reranker is BERT-base finetuned on 6k labeled q|d pairs.
Evaluation results: reranker improves clinical relevance (BLEU/NDCG proxies) but doubles latency at top-5. Team asking for quantized re-ranker or offload pattern to reduce p95.
Indexing scale: target scope ~18,000,000 documents (avg doc length 1.8k tokens), ~1.2B tokens total; expected growth 25%/yr.
Traffic profile: 100–200 QPS peak across global sites; most queries require < 250ms server-side latency for interactive clinician workflows.
Cost target: internal benchmark <$0.005 per query (embeddings + retrieval + rerank amortized), currently at ~$0.011 with current model mix.
Model preferences: prefer quantized open models for on-prem (Llama-family 13B/34B quantized), want hosted fallback to smaller open weights for surge capacity.
Routing/fallback ask: automatic fallback to lower-cost model with clear drift/quality monitoring; require pinning of model versions per environment.
Integration: EHR connectors (HL7/FHIR) will be handled by internal ETL; need Redwood private control plane with VPC peering, HSM/KMS integration, and detailed access logs.
Quote from Head of Informatics: 'If you can hit our latency and audit requirements and keep costs predictable, we can pilot 2 hospitals.'
Blocker notes: legal wants explicit retention SLA for audit logs and clarification on ephemeral cache purging for PHI-containing KV caches.
Suggested Redwood play: run Dedicated POC with 1) quantized reranker on A100-pinned pool, 2) prefix/KV caching enabled, 3) token-level cost telemetry for two weeks.
